Shows your **TechnoVE** EV charging station (Quebec-made i-Series,
s-Series) in Gladys through its **local API**: no cloud, no account,
straight on your network.

> **Unofficial API, never tested with a real station.**
> Not affiliated with TechnoVE. The integration talks to the local API of the station like the
> python-technove library (used by Home Assistant). TechnoVE may change it
> without notice.

## What you get

One device per station with:

| Feature                  | Content                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Status                   | Unplugged, Plugged in waiting, Charging, faults, outside the activation period, high tariff |
| Connector                | Available, occupied, faulted or unavailable (Gladys "charging station" category)            |
| Charging state           | Charging, vehicle connected, paused (charging not allowed), idle                            |
| Power (estimated)        | In W: current × output voltage (the station gives no power)                                 |
| Current                  | In A                                                                                        |
| Input and output voltage | In V                                                                                        |
| Energy of the session    | In kWh, a plain sensor                                                                      |
| Maximum current          | In A, the current setting of the station                                                    |
| Charging allowed         | Yes / no                                                                                    |
| Automatic charging       | Yes / no (set in the TechnoVE app)                                                          |
| Load sharing             | Yes / no, and "load sharing conflict": read only                                            |
| Start charging           | Button (commands allowed only)                                                              |
| Stop charging            | Button (commands allowed only)                                                              |
| Set the maximum current  | List from 8 A to the rating of the station (commands allowed only)                          |

Read every 30 seconds by default (10 s to 10 min, configurable).

**Energy**: the energy of the session is a **plain sensor**, never an index:
it does not enter the Energy tab of Gladys (the station is already counted by
your main meter). No daily consumption is published.

## Installation

1. Give the station a **fixed IP address** in your router.
2. Install the integration from the Gladys store.
3. In its configuration, enter the **IP address of the station** (several
   stations in load sharing: separated by commas, four at most).
4. Save, then add the station from the **Discovery** tab.

The **Test the connection** button reads each station once (at most every
10 seconds). The local API has no password: any machine of your network can
read it, Gladys included.

## Commands (off by default)

"Start charging", "Stop charging" and "Set the maximum current" refuse
every command while **Allow the commands** is off. On:

- **Start** allows the charge (the vehicle charges as soon as it asks);
  refused when the station reports a fault or an unknown state;
- **Stop** forbids the charge;
- **Maximum current**: from 8 A to the rating the station reports
  (`maxStationCurrent`), in whole amperes.

Start and stop are refused while **automatic charging** is on (a setting of
the TechnoVE app); the maximum current is refused in **load sharing** (the
sharing sets it).

They are **buttons** and a **list**, never switches: a "turn everything
off" (from Gladys, Google Home, Alexa or HomeKit) never reaches them. A
scene can trigger them, only through an explicit action, and only when the
commands are allowed. Note that the AI chat of Gladys (MCP) can create and
run such a scene: while the commands are allowed, it can start or stop the
charge.

Before each command, the integration **reads the station again** and decides
on that read only; the option is checked again right before sending. A
command with nothing to do (already so) is not sent. A command that cannot
leave within 3.5 seconds is refused unsent. When the station does not
confirm (silence, a 5xx error), Gladys shows "Command sent, without
confirmation": check the state, read again 5 then 20 seconds later. One
command at a time per station: another one is refused at once, except a
**stop**, never blocked: it waits for the command in flight only as long as
its own deadline allows, then goes; it is sent once more when that command
ends, and a start not sent yet gives way to it.

## Errors and limits

- **Station unreachable**: only the connector ("unavailable") and the
  status ("Station unreachable") change; the power, the current, the
  charging state and the other values keep their last value (a "charging"
  may stay shown: check the status). A station removed from the
  configuration, or that never answered since the start, shows the same on
  its device, and the configuration screen names it. New try after 30 s,
  1, 2, then 5 minutes, never faster than the interval.
- **429 (too many requests)**, unlikely on a local station: a pause of 1
  minute to 6 hours for everything (reads, button, commands), never shorter
  than the refresh interval, kept in `/data` across a restart.
- The **power is estimated** (current × voltage, power factor assumed to be
  1): the station does not give it.
- Neither the schedule (off-peak / high tariff), nor the automatic charge,
  nor the maximum charge percentage can be changed from Gladys.
- The logs never hold the text of the station's answers.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt TechnoVE in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your TechnoVE station | `section` | Nein | Shows your TechnoVE charging station in Gladys through its local API, without any cloud: status (unplugged, plugged in and waiting, charging, faults), power (estimated), current, voltages, energy of the session, maximum current and load sharing. Enter the IP address of the station (give it a fixed address in your router), save, then add it from the Discovery tab. Starting, stopping and the maximum current can be changed from Gladys only if you allow the commands below. Unofficial API, never tested with a real station. Not affiliated with TechnoVE. |
| IP address of the station | `string` | Ja | An IPv4 address or a host name. Several stations (load sharing): separate them with commas, four at most. |
| Allow the commands | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default. On: Gladys may start and stop the charge and set the maximum current (8 A to the rating of the station). Off: these three features refuse every command. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | Nein | How often each station is read, in seconds. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | Nein | Used for the feature names of the devices added from now on, for the status texts and for the command errors. |

## So installierst du TechnoVE in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: TechnoVE erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-technove:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-technove](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-technove).

TechnoVE benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

TechnoVE ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
